observation.visible_scene: A vertical white sealant/caulk tube (black text label, small green logo panel) is held above a glossy black reflective surface, its nozzle pressed to the seam where the surface meets a white edge. A continuous white bead of extruded sealant runs from the nozzle diagonally down toward the right edge of the frame, and a second already-laid white line runs along the top-right back edge. A mirror reflection of the tube, nozzle and bead is visible on the dark surface below, with a blurred dark hand/finger shape at the bottom center.
visible_changes: The white bead remains attached to the nozzle throughout, indicating ongoing extrusion along the seam rather than a one-time deposit.
The tube and nozzle assembly drift slowly leftward and slightly upward within the frame; the leading tip of the bead moves with the nozzle while the previously laid portion stays on the surface.
The reflection of the tube/nozzle tracks the tube's position, confirming it is a mirror image and not a second object.

The on-screen angle and length of the diagonal bead line change gradually (it becomes steeper/longer toward the right edge), and the top-right background line shifts relative to the nozzle, consistent with a slow camera pan/tilt or the operator translating along the seam.
The visible portion of the tube label changes (more of the black text block, then less), indicating a slight rotation or vertical shift of the tube.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the bead-laying began before this excerpt or continues after it; the full extent of the seam and the surrounding surface are not shown.
What material the sealant is and what the black surface is made of.
Whether the framing change is camera motion, operator motion, or both.
uncertain_details: The exact cause of the changing perspective (camera movement vs. the tube being drawn along the edge) cannot be separated confidently from the sparse background.
The identity of the dark shape at the bottom (hand vs. reflection artifact) is partly obscured.
